title: By His Wounds You Have Been Healed
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: Jesus' death brings freedom from sin, his wounds bring healing, and because he rose, we have a Shepherd who is always with us.
exhortation: Jesus' death brings freedom. He took our sins on himself and was willingly nailed to a tree. Our sin has been defeated, and our great enemy has been destroyed. Our victory over sin is found in the sacrificial death of Christ.

His wounds bring healing. Because he was wounded and pierced for us, our wounds, emotional or physical, will be healed and are healed, including the wounds we carry in our relationships. Jesus was wounded for our transgressions and rose to victorious life.

And because he died for our sins and rose again, we have a Shepherd who is always with us. We have protection, guidance and provision. Like a shepherd with his sheep, Jesus provides for our every need and gives us direction.

I was reading in Numbers recently, where the law addresses the death penalty. It says you may not ransom the life of someone who has taken a life, because when blood is spilled, only blood can pay for it. And the precious blood of Jesus has paid for it. It should have been our blood. It should have been our wounds. But because he was wounded and bled for us, we are set free, we are healed, and we have a Shepherd who protects, provides and guides us.
prayer: Lord, we thank you for the blood. Your sacrifice worked. It was effective. It is finished. You took every blow, fulfilled every prophecy and lived a perfect life. Your death was fully sufficient for the forgiveness of our sins.

I pray for anyone listening who has not put their faith and trust in you, that their sins would be forgiven. I pray they would trust right now in the saving work of your blood poured out for them. And for those of us who call you Lord and King, may we remember, and find fresh strength and courage for the mission you've given us here on earth, until the day you return or we go home to you. In Jesus' name, amen.
